observation.title: FOS-000001 — Preserve precise context in existing diagnostics
observation.body:
Legacy identity: `FOS-000001`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

Shared requirements and grouping: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/8. All original criteria below remain required. Source status statements below describe their historical revision; current delivery evidence is recorded separately. Original relative links are resolved below.

## Original definition (verbatim)

1. **FOS-000001 — Preserve precise context in existing diagnostics.** **S; no dependencies; §5.** Pipeline creation failure logs discard the available `VkResult` at [replay:1559](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L1559), with analogous compute/ray-tracing branches. Device setup similarly reduces failures to prose. Include phase, resource type/hash and raw numeric result; capture `errno`/`GetLastError()` immediately at OS failures. Fix compute/ray-tracing capture messages incorrectly naming graphics/compute in [dispatch:918](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/layer/dispatch.cpp#L918) and nearby ray-tracing paths. Start with these sites, then extend per subsystem. **Check:** inject distinct Vulkan results and verify distinguishable evidence. Do not classify every non-success as a driver crash or every capture rejection as unsupported pNext. This delivers immediate value before a common schema exists.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Unit tests with Vulkan/OS failure injection:** Distinct injected Vulkan results and OS errors retain their exact numeric values, phase and known resource identity after cleanup; an intervening OS call cannot overwrite the originating error.
   - **Captured-diagnostic assertions:** Compute and ray-tracing failures name the correct resource type. Controlled Vulkan errors and capture rejections do not claim a driver crash or unsupported feature without evidence; a successful control case emits no failure diagnostic.

<!-- fossilize-migration-v1:FOS-000001 -->

observation.title: FOS-000004 — Retain unrecoverable child loss in the controller
observation.body:
Legacy identity: `FOS-000004`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

Shared requirements and grouping: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/8. All original criteria below remain required. Source status statements below describe their historical revision; current delivery evidence is recorded separately. Original relative links are resolved below.

## Original definition (verbatim)

4. **FOS-000004 — Retain unrecoverable child loss in the controller.** **S–M; no dependencies; §2–§4.** [Linux shutdown:335](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L335) and [Windows shutdown:278](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp#L278) use the same boolean for “do not restart because done” and “cannot continue.” Their callers restart conditionally but otherwise continue to exit success ([Linux:1429](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L1429), [Windows:1035](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp#L1035)). Separate restart disposition from the retained worker outcome. Immediately return an aggregate unsuccessful result when assigned required work is unresolved. **Check:** E5/E6; clean worker; failed worker alongside a clean worker; failure before resource identity is known. Record the assigned range and unknown remainder. Do not fail all successfully recovered attempts just because a child once died.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Controller subprocess tests on Linux and Windows:** A worker lost before its first progress report produces an unsuccessful controller outcome, retaining its assigned range and unknown remainder. Repeat with another worker succeeding and with worker report order reversed; the unsuccessful aggregate is unchanged.
   - **Recovery control tests:** Clean completion succeeds; a failed attempt followed by verified completion of every required item can succeed. A skipped required culprit or unresolved range cannot succeed. Assert the controller result directly, independently of stderr and optional shared progress.

<!-- fossilize-migration-v1:FOS-000004 -->

observation.title: FOS-000005 — Separate replay-thread work completion from item success
observation.body:
Legacy identity: `FOS-000005`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

Shared requirements and grouping: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/8. All original criteria below remain required. Source status statements below describe their historical revision; current delivery evidence is recorded separately. Original relative links are resolved below.

## Original definition (verbatim)

5. **FOS-000005 — Separate replay-thread work completion from item success.** **M; depends on `FOS-000001` and `FOS-000004` for complete propagation; §2–§3.** [worker:1800](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L1800) discards the parse return and increments `completed_count` after processing; creation helpers return void. [normal replay:4553](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L4553) returns success after the queue finishes (E7). Introduce a thread-safe outcome accumulator independent of optional shared memory. First cover parse/read and Vulkan creation failures, then setup/validation/support/dependency exits. Propagate the result through normal replay, child and controller. **Check:** E7, missing entry, injected Vulkan failure, and mixed success/failure. Keep queue progress as queue progress. Unsupported required work must be unsuccessful under the declared policy, even when it is not a crash.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Replay unit and CLI integration tests:** E7, missing input entries, injected creation errors, unsupported required work, validation failures and dependency-blocked work produce the expected distinct outcomes and nonzero aggregate exits. A fully successful workload returns zero.
   - **Thread/mode matrix:** The same fixed mixed workload has the same final logical outcome in normal, child/controller and progress modes, with shared progress absent/present and one/multiple threads. Queue completion still reaches its expected count even when processing fails; it is never the success oracle.

<!-- fossilize-migration-v1:FOS-000005 -->

observation.title: FOS-000007 — Record timeout origin before invoking crash recovery
observation.body:
Legacy identity: `FOS-000007`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

Shared requirements and grouping: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/8. All original criteria below remain required. Source status statements below describe their historical revision; current delivery evidence is recorded separately. Original relative links are resolved below.

## Original definition (verbatim)

7. **FOS-000007 — Record timeout origin before invoking crash recovery.** **S–M; depends on `FOS-000004`; §4–§5.** [no-progress wait:965](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L965) invokes the timeout handler before its diagnostic. [Linux:1589](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L1589) sends SIGABRT; [Windows:1203](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp#L1203) writes `CRASH`. Store/send a distinct trigger from the healthy dispatcher before termination. Distinguish configured work-no-progress timeout, controller heartbeat timeout, and post-crash cleanup timeout. Include actual monotonic elapsed time and configured threshold. **Check:** deterministic no-progress injection, spontaneous fault, heartbeat loss, failed signal delivery and escalation. An externally observed SIGKILL alone does not prove a controller timeout or OOM. Multiple threads imply unknown individual attribution unless independently established.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Fake-clock and termination-adapter unit tests:** Each configured no-progress, heartbeat and cleanup deadline records its own trigger, threshold and monotonic elapsed time before requesting termination. Progress resets only the applicable deadline; a spontaneous fault has no invented timeout trigger.
   - **Controller integration tests:** Injected SIGABRT/Windows recovery, failed termination delivery and escalation preserve trigger, mechanism and final effect separately. An unexplained external SIGKILL remains unattributed; multi-thread cases without item evidence retain unknown attribution. Use synchronization barriers, not timing races, to order events.

<!-- fossilize-migration-v1:FOS-000007 -->

observation.title: FOS-000008 — Reject malformed resource envelopes as controlled input errors
observation.body:
Legacy identity: `FOS-000008`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

Shared requirements and grouping: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/8. All original criteria below remain required. Source status statements below describe their historical revision; current delivery evidence is recorded separately. Original relative links are resolved below.

## Original definition (verbatim)

8. **FOS-000008 — Reject malformed resource envelopes as controlled input errors.** **S for envelope guard, M for nested validation; depends on `FOS-000001` and `FOS-000005`; §1–§2.** [parse:6368](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize.cpp#L6368) indexes `doc["version"].GetInt()` without checking object/member/type (E5). Start with the envelope, reporting invalid shape versus incompatible version; audit nested field reads in subsequent bounded patches. Preserve numeric parse error/offset and resource identity without dumping shader contents. **Check:** `{}`, `[]`, null, missing/string version, malformed nested records; none may assert, terminate the embedding host or be blamed on the driver. Test release and debug builds. This is an outcome/containment prerequisite, not merely prettier logging; no claim of a complete parser-security audit is made here.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Parser table tests in debug and release builds:** Null, arrays, {}, missing/wrong-type version, invalid JSON and malformed nested fixtures for every migrated parser return controlled reason-bearing errors without assertions, signals or host termination. Incompatible numeric versions have a different reason from malformed shape.
   - **Containment and input-mutation tests:** A subprocess sentinel continues after each rejected input; valid fixtures still parse identically. A fixed-seed mutation corpus is run automatically with a bounded runtime, and newly found failures become deterministic fixtures. Diagnostics expose available error offsets/identity but no shader payload.

<!-- fossilize-migration-v1:FOS-000008 -->

observation.title: FOS-000009 — Carry reason data from the place that detects it
observation.body:
Legacy identity: `FOS-000009`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

Shared requirements and grouping: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/8. All original criteria below remain required. Source status statements below describe their historical revision; current delivery evidence is recorded separately. Original relative links are resolved below.

## Original definition (verbatim)

9. **FOS-000009 — Carry reason data from the place that detects it.** **M; depends on `FOS-000005`, `FOS-000007`, `FOS-000008`; §1, §4–§5.** Add a small stable internal result/event representation: phase, reason ID, known raw error, tag/hash or range, worker and attempt, plus unknown-context flags. Start with parse, creation and timeout paths. Extend child messages on both platforms with explicit framing/version negotiation and bounded parsing; never require the controller to infer categories from human logs. **Check:** split/truncated messages, unknown version/reason, missing final message, worker exit before first report. Unknown information stays unknown. This is where downstream controllers acquire causes; a parent-only summary cannot recover details a worker never sends.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Result serialization and streaming-parser unit tests:** Each migrated producer preserves reason, phase, raw error and applicable identity through a round trip. Feed every split position, multiple records per read, truncated/oversized records and unknown versions/reasons; parsing stays bounded and never converts absent context into known values.
   - **Worker/controller integration tests:** With worker prose disabled, injected parse, creation and timeout failures remain distinguishable at the controller. Death before the first report and loss of the final report yield explicit uncertainty rather than fabricated resource identity or success.

<!-- fossilize-migration-v1:FOS-000009 -->

observation.title: FOS-000011 — Expose discovery and selection completeness
observation.body:
Legacy identity: `FOS-000011`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

Shared requirements and grouping: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/8. All original criteria below remain required. Source status statements below describe their historical revision; current delivery evidence is recorded separately. Original relative links are resolved below.

## Original definition (verbatim)

11. **FOS-000011 — Expose discovery and selection completeness.** **M; depends on `FOS-000009`; §2.** [stream scanning:1200](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize_db.cpp#L1200) intentionally salvages truncated tails (E9). Database composites may omit unavailable inputs; whitelists/ranges and replay-cache checks change observable work. Return preparation/discovery metadata: requested/opened inputs, excluded inputs/items with policy, selected logical scope, truncation/read failures, complete/unknown discovery. Keep salvage behavior and report its limits. **Check:** intact empty archive versus truncated archive with zero retained entries; missing optional versus required subdatabase; filters and ranges. Known processed items cannot establish full coverage when unread scope is unknown. A caller may explicitly accept a recovered prefix, but the report must name that scope.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Database/discovery integration tests:** E9 reports incomplete discovery even with zero retained items, while an intact empty archive reports known complete empty scope. The intact prefix remains readable; required missing/unreadable inputs prevent full-scope success.
   - **Selection/policy table tests:** Ranges, whitelists, deliberately optional inputs and explicitly accepted recovered-prefix policy report the exact selected/excluded scope and policy. Unknown unread totals remain unknown, never zero or full coverage; excluded items are not counted as failures or successes.

<!-- fossilize-migration-v1:FOS-000011 -->

observation.title: Observability: preserve trustworthy outcomes across Fossilize
observation.body:
Required outcome: deliver every migrated observability child with its original criteria. This epic stays open until all required children and shared gates complete.

## Ordered implementation backlog

All criteria below are mandatory completion gates for the applicable implementation slice. They describe future assertions, not tests already implemented or passing. A task is complete only when its criteria are covered by committed automated tests registered with the project test runner/CI, and passing evidence records the commands, configurations and platforms. If a task is split, each split-out item must receive its own registered key and name its covered criteria; the parent remains incomplete until all are satisfied. Manual inspection, log screenshots and the observation-only research runner are insufficient acceptance evidence.

Use unit tests for result/state logic and deterministic fault injection, plus subprocess/filesystem/IPC/layer integration tests for externally visible behavior. Assert returned outcomes, exit statuses, structured fields, actual output contents and handle/application behavior; prose-only assertions are appropriate only where human presentation itself is the requirement. Include successful controls alongside failure cases. Upgrade E1–E9 into assertion-bearing regressions as their owning tasks are implemented. Tests must expose the defect before its fix where feasible, rather than merely mirror implementation internals.

Concurrency/deadline tests must use fake clocks, barriers and controllable adapters instead of random driver instability or fragile sleeps. Give process tests watchdogs and isolated temporary output directories. Linux and Windows process changes require platform-specific automated evidence; GPU-independent mocks are the baseline, with hardware jobs for hardware claims. An unavailable platform/device is skipped/unverified and leaves that acceptance criterion open. Record applicable debug/release and exception-enabled/disabled coverage; use sanitizer jobs where useful for changed parsing, lifetime or concurrency code. Tests must check honest unknown outcomes where evidence is deliberately lost.

**Compatibility gate for every affected public boundary:** declare whether source, binary, protocol and behavioral compatibility are preserved or intentionally changed. Maintain compile/run fixtures for preserved old callers/invocations, schema/protocol fixtures for preserved consumers and prebuilt-consumer checks only where binary compatibility is claimed. Assert and document intentional changes, including formerly false-success CLI exits. Additive signatures alone do not establish compatibility; do not claim that all existing callers continue working. Require structured outcomes without prose parsing once the relevant result API/mode is introduced.


## Dependency and delivery notes

The critical path is **FOS-000005 → FOS-000009 → (FOS-000010 and FOS-000011) → FOS-000012 → FOS-000013 → FOS-000014**: worker facts precede reconciliation, which precedes a trustworthy controller/API result. **FOS-000003 → FOS-000016 → FOS-000017 → FOS-000019** is the persistence/capture path. **FOS-000006** prevents later runs from trusting a failed attempt. **FOS-000004** is an early containment fix, not a substitute for the richer accounting. Initial result schemas may report persistence/support detail as unknown until the respective producers are migrated; they must not imply whole-standard compliance early.

Keep regression verification alongside every iteration. Do not defer all tests to `FOS-000024`. The highest-value fixtures are E1–E9, deterministic worker failure/deadline injection, duplicate/stale messages, full diagnostic rings, close-time ENOSPC, optional versus required output loss, and cancellation before/after final publication. Linux and Windows process implementations need the same behavioral matrix even when mechanisms differ. Apple/Android builds use `NO_ROBUST_REPLAYER`; ordinary replay/library/capture contracts still apply without inventing worker support there.


## Remaining verification

Before implementation is accepted, run supported CMake builds and tests on Linux and Windows, exception-enabled/disabled and release/debug configurations as applicable. Add deterministic fault injection rather than relying solely on the existing random `SIMULATE_UNSTABLE_DRIVER` hooks. Exercise runtime capture with multiple instances/devices and real Vulkan support failures; test cache feedback on hardware that exposes it. No current probe demonstrates actual cache warming or durable driver output.


## Unkeyed report disposition
# Repeated shader processing with unclear failure and cache-reuse outcomes

The Sims 4 repeatedly delayed startup with “Processing Vulkan shaders,” despite previous processing having finished.

Steam launched Fossilize’s replayer before Proton, with a **10-second limit without pipeline completion**. Controlled tests showed workers timing out and compilation being interrupted. Allowing 60 seconds let the tested workload finish; its resulting cache was reusable.

The investigation was complicated by several observability gaps:

- **Hidden failure context:** Steam’s normal logs showed progress and completion without an actionable explanation of worker failures. Separate, unsuppressed replay runs exposed the timeouts.
- **Ambiguous crash reporting:** Timeouts used SIGABRT and the crash-recovery path. A debugger was needed to establish that an interrupted worker was executing inside NVIDIA’s shader compiler; this did not prove a spontaneous driver crash.
- **Unclear completion:** One replay returned exit status zero despite reporting “Cannot continue,” making successful termination insufficient evidence of completed work.
- **Unclear reuse:** The logs did not clearly connect replay triggers, previously processed entries, skipped/failed work and persisted results. A shader-bucket update also triggered processing of an unchanged generic database.

**The integration gap:** Fossilize needs to expose explicit failure reasons and partial outcomes even in quiet mode. Steam needs to retain and present those results alongside why replay was scheduled and what reuse information is available.

The investigation did **not** establish that the entire cache was discarded. Cache reuse worked in controlled tests, while deliberately forcing a warm replay still incurred substantial processing overhead.

## References

Investigated 26–27 October 2026.

- [Upstream issue: steam-for-linux #13810](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-for-linux/issues/13810)
- [Sanitized supporting evidence](https://gist.github.com/robinwassen/6d8cd12e4040cf409cb3553f4fb87b61)

Fossilize obligations overlap FOS-000004/000005/000007/000009/000012/000013/000014/000022; retained individually without a duplicate issue. Steam scheduling/presentation belongs to external steam-for-linux#13810; no new Fossilize implementation requirement.

Specifications, reproduced E1..E9 findings, adversarial review and sanitized fixtures are supporting evidence, not additional task definitions.
